children.translated_text: Pervading all particular states of being, moving and unmoving, made of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>), one, infinite, without beginning,
I worship in my heart the Lord <s>Bhairava</s>, refuge of the shelterless, with a mind absorbed in you. ||1||

children.text: tvanmayam etad aśeṣam idānīṃ bhāti mama tvadanugrahaśaktyā |
children.translated_text: All this without remainder now shines for me as pervaded by you, through the power of your grace (<s>anugraha</s>);

children.text: tvaṃ ca maheśa sadaiva mamātmā svātmamayaṃ mama tena samastam ||
children.translated_text: and you, O <s>Maheśa</s> (Great Lord), are forever my Self—therefore everything for me is made of my own Self. ||2||

children.text: svātmani viśvagaye tvayi nāthe tena na saṃsṛtibhītikathāsti |
children.translated_text: Since you, the Lord, are present everywhere as my own Self, there is therefore no talk of fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence),
even when masses of <s>karma</s> exist that create unbearable suffering, delusion, and terror. ||3||

children.text: antaka māṃ prati mā dṛśam enāṃ krodhakarālatamāṃ vinidhehi |
children.translated_text: O <s>Antaka</s> (Death)! Do not cast upon me this gaze most terrible with wrath—
I am steadfast in the worship and contemplation of <s>Śaṅkara</s>; I am filled with the power of the terrifying <s>Bhairava</s>! ||4||
Thus, with the great darkness torn asunder by the rays of consciousness pervaded by you,

children.text: mṛtyuyamāntakakarmapiśācair nātha namo 'stu na jātu bibhemi ||
children.translated_text: O Lord, homage to you! I never fear <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), <s>Yama</s>, <s>Antaka</s> (the Ender), or the demons of <s>karma</s>. ||5||
Having perceived the true nature of all worldly things through the risen rays of true awakening,

children.text: bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇe tvayy aham ātmani nirvṛtim emi ||
children.translated_text: in you, the Self, who are full and overflowing with the supreme nectar of being—I attain bliss (<s>nirvṛti</s>). ||6||
Whenever the condition of <s>kleśa</s> (affliction), which creates intense torment, comes within the range of the mind,
O Lord, at that very moment the supreme nectar-rain of this hymn of non-difference from you rises for me. ||7||
O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, this is truth: vows, gifts, bathing, and austerity destroy the torment of worldly existence;
but meditation on the supreme nectar of your <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) pours forth a stream of bliss in the mind. ||8||

children.text: nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati gāḍhaṃ saṃvid iyaṃ mama bhairavanātha |
children.translated_text: This consciousness of mine dances, sings, and deeply rejoices, O Lord <s>Bhairava</s>,

children.text: tvāṃ priyam āpya sudarśanam ekaṃ durlabham anyajanaiḥ samayajñam ||
children.translated_text: having attained you, the beloved one, of beautiful form, the one, difficult for others to attain, the knower of the sacred tradition (<s>samaya</s>). ||9||

children.text: vasurasapauṣe kṛṣṇadaśamyām abhinavaguptaḥ stavam imam akarot |
children.translated_text: In [the month of] <s>Pauṣa</s> of the year <s>Vasu-Rasa</s>, on the dark tenth (<s>kṛṣṇadaśamī</s>), <s>Abhinavagupta</s> composed this hymn,

children.text: yena vibhur bhavamarusantāpaṃ śamayati janasya jhaṭiti dayāluḥ ||
children.translated_text: by which the all-pervading and compassionate Lord swiftly cools the scorching heat of worldly existence for people.
This hymn named after <s>Abhinava</s>, consisting of nine verses (<s>padyanavaka</s>), is completed.
